en: The *Buddhōṣṇīṣa-mahā-sitātapatrā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
translated by the Imperial Edict by the Tripitaka Master Śaraba, Grand Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Great Minister of Education.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the Sudharmā Hall of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven,
together with a great assembly of bhikṣus, great bodhisattvas, Śakra, Lord of Devas, and countless other beings.
At that time, the Bhagavān spread his seat and sat down;
he immediately entered the Samādhi of the Universal Observation of the Uṣṇīṣa.
Then, from the uṣṇīṣa on the crown of his head, the Bhagavān suddenly [emerged].
To perform the secret and subtle practice of the Dharma:
Homage to all Buddhas and the assembly of all great Bodhisattvas!
Homage to the Buddha!
Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Saṅgha!
Homage to the seven koṭis of Buddhas and their great assembly of śrāvakas!
Homage to all the Arhats in the world;
homage to all those who have entered the stream;
homage to all those who have attained the stage of once-returning.
Homage to all the assembly of Non-returners.
Homage to the assembly of those who practice correctly in the world.
Homage to the assembly of those who are heading toward correct practice.
Homage to the great hosts of celestial ṛṣis who are able to bring benefit even through curses and incantations.
Homage to the hosts of accomplished vidyādharas.
Homage to the hosts of the Great Brahmā Deva King.
Homage to the assembly of Śakra, Lord of the Devas;
homage to the assembly of Rudra, Umāpati, and Śikhīśvara;
homage to the assembly that pays reverence with the five great mudrās of the Son Without Attachment.
Homage to the Mother who destroys the cities of the three realms and delights in the cold forest, who is venerated by the hosts of mahākālas.
Homage to the Bhagavat Tathāgata Kūṭarāja. Homage to Padmakūṭarāja.
Homage to Vajrakumāra! Homage to Ratnakumāra! Homage to Mahāgajakumāra!
Homage to Kumāra! Homage to Nāgodbhava-kumāra!
Homage to the Bhagavān Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vīravīrya-kula-śastra-rāja Buddha!
Homage to the Bhagavān, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitābha Buddha.
Homage to the Bhagavān, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya Buddha.
Homage to the Bhagavān, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabharāja Buddha.
Homage to the Bhagavān, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śālavṛkṣapuṣpasaṃkusumitarāja Buddha.
Homage to the Bhagavān, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni Buddha.
Homage to the Bhagavān, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnaketurāja Buddha.
Homage to the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, Samantabhadra-rāja Buddha.
Homage to the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vairocana Buddha.
Homage to the Bhagavān, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vipulākṣa-utpala-gandha-dhvaja-rāja Buddha. Having thus paid homage to these Buddhas and others, [one should proceed].
The Bhagavatī Uṣṇīṣaśītāntapatrā is invincible;
Prajñācārī can extinguish all bhūtas and malevolent spirits.
It cuts off all secret mantras and liberates one from bondage;
it keeps one far removed from untimely death, distress, and evil dreams;
and it destroys the eighty-four thousand malevolent spirits and the eight planetary deities.
Furthermore, it can cause the twenty-eight lunar mansions to give rise to great joy;
it can also turn back all enmity and harm, as well as all those who intend to inflict poison or injury.
She causes all evil dreams to be utterly extinguished.
She is further able to rescue and eliminate the perils of poison, weapons, water, fire, and so forth.
Possessing unrivaled great power, she is the Mother of Violent and Great Might.
The Mother of Blazing Majestic Radiance; the White Parasol Mother of Great Power;
the Mother with the Garland of Flames and the White-Robed Mother; Tārā with the Constricted Face and the Garland of Proportions;
the Victorious Vajra; the Lotus-Marked One and the Vajra-Marked One.
Possessing garlands, invincible, the Mother who shatters the vajra wall,
revered by all virtuous deities; the Mother of great majesty and splendor who delivers [beings],
the powerful one, together with the vajra shackles and their equals.
The lineage of Vajrakumāra; the lineage of the Vajra-holder, Suvarṇamālā, and the mother Ratnolkā of ruddy hue;
the radiant Vajramālā, the slender mother who holds a vajra; and the mother whose eyes are like golden light.
Vajraprabhā said to the Mother: "May the mudrās of Padmasūryaprabha and the assembly of all vows protect me!
May they protect me! Oṃ riṣkana parasaṃtāya sarvatathāgata uṣṇīṣa..."

*Roḥ* (8) *sarvaduṣṭānāṃ* (9) *stambhana-kari hūṃ droṅ* (10) *sarvayakṣarākṣasagrahāṇāṃ* *vidhvaṃsana-kari hūṃ droṅ* (10) *caṇḍoṣitānāṃ* (10) *grahasaṃhārāṇāṃ* (10) *vidhvaṃsana-kari hūṃ droḥ*.
Oṃ āśiṣṭapraśāntināthānāṃ prasadana-kari hūṃ dharoṃ | Oṃ āśitanāṃ mahākrodhānāṃ vidhvaṃsana-kari hūṃ dharoṃ | Oṃ rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ | May you protect me! May you protect me!
She possesses hundreds of thousands of koṭis of eyes;
she is the Vajra Great Mother of vast proportions, whose mark is the blazing non-duality,
having attained great sovereignty within the triple world.
May you protect me! May you protect me!
Oṃ! Fear of kings, fear of thieves and bandits, fear of fire, fear of water, fear of poison, fear of weapons, and fear of invasion by enemy armies.
Fear of famine, fear of harm from enemies, fear of pestilence, fear of thunderbolts;
fear of untimely and accidental death, fear of earthquakes, fear of malevolent stars;
fear of hell, fear of devas, fear of nāgas, fear of lightning, fear of flying spirits, and fear of wild beasts.
Furthermore, there are celestial spirits, dragon spirits, asura spirits;
wind-god spirits, sky-flying spirits, incense-seeking spirits, human and non-human spirits;
large-bellied wandering spirits, obstructing spirits, rākṣasa spirits, and preta spirits.
The ḍākinīs, the flesh-eating bhūtas,
the jar-bellied spirits, the stinking ghosts, the foul-smelling ghosts,
the saṃketa spirits, the forgetfulness spirits, and the epilepsy spirits.
May the māras, the enchanters, the vaśīkaraṇas, and the pāṭanas,
as well as all malevolent spirits, grant me peace and security.
Furthermore, may those who consume the gods and those who consume vital essence [protect me].
Those who eat embryos, those who eat blood, those who eat fat;
those who eat flesh, those who eat marrow, those who eat bones;
those who eat the newborn, those who take life, and those who eat vomit.
Those who eat impure things: those who eat urine, those who eat leaking water,
those who eat leftover food, those who eat vomit, those who eat saliva,
those who eat nasal mucus, those who eat pus, and those who eat alms-food.
Those who feed on garlands, those who feed on perfumes, those who feed on fragrances;
those who seize the mind, those who feed on flowers, those who feed on fruits;
those who feed on the five grains, those who feed on burnt offerings—among all these, may I be at peace.
All such assemblies as these, as well as the vidyā-mantras created by various malevolent spirits,
shall be completely eradicated;
they shall be pinned down with vajra-stakes.
The vidyā-mantras created by the *sarvatraga* [deities] are all completely severed and pinned down with vajra-nails;
the vidyā-mantras created by the *ḍāka*s and *ḍākinī*s—
All are completely severed and the adamantine stakes are driven in.
All the vidyā-mantras created by Mahāpārṣadī are completely severed and the adamantine stakes are driven in.
The vidyā-mantras created by the sons of Māra are all completely severed and pinned down with vajra-stakes;
so too are the vidyā-mantras created by the hosts of those who fly through the air.
All are completely severed and pinned down with vajra-stakes.
The vidyā-mantras created by the mahākāla and the hosts of mātṛ spirits are all completely severed and pinned down with vajra-stakes.
The vidyā-mantras created by those who carry skulls are all utterly severed and pinned down with vajra-nails;
they are able to overcome the vidyā-mantras created by those who perform the "honey-making" rites and accomplish various worldly tasks.
All [these] are completely severed by the Vajra-Nail;
the vidyā-mantras created by the assembly of the four sisters are all completely severed by the Vajra-Crown-Nail.
The vidyā-mantras composed by the hosts such as Vikṛti, Kāmarati, Īśvara,
and Gaṇapati are all severed and pinned down with vajra-nails;
likewise, the vidyā-mantras composed by Nagnajit.
All [these] are completely severed and the vajra-stakes are driven in.
The vidyā-mantras created by arhats are all completely severed and the vajra-stakes are driven in.
The vidyā-mantras created by those free from desire are all severed and pinned down with vajra-stakes;
so too are the vidyā-mantras created by Guhyapada Vajrapāṇi.
May all [obstacles] be completely severed and the vajra-stakes be driven in. Homage to the Bhagavatī, the Great White Parasol of the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa! May she protect me, may she protect me!

If there should be any sentient beings who give rise to a mind of malice toward me...
Furthermore, there are those who give rise to a mind of resentment,
those who give rise to a mind of malice, and those who give rise to a mind of violence and cruelty.
The hosts of celestial māras,
the hosts of nāga māras,
and the hosts of asura māras.
The host of wind spirits,
the host of those who fly through the air,
and the host of those who seek out fragrances.
The hosts of human and non-human spirits,
the hosts of great-bellied wandering spirits,
and the hosts of yakṣas;
The hosts of rākṣasa-māras,
the hosts of preta-māras,
and the hosts of ḍākinī-māras.
The host of flesh-eating mātarah,
the host of mātarah with bellies like jars, and the host of mātarah with bloated bellies.
The hosts of foul-scented malevolent spirits, the hosts of variously foul-scented malevolent spirits,
and the hosts of *sai-kien-ta* (*saindhava*) malevolent spirits.
The host of *huīn* demons,
the host of *diān* demons,
and the host of *yàn* demons.
The host of subduing māras,
the host of *ṛṣi-māras*,
and the host of Yama-māras.
The *śakunī* spirits,
the *mātṛkā* spirits, the *rākṣasī* spirits,
and the *vyālarākṣasī* spirits.
It removes the hosts of thorn-demons (kaṇṭakāmanuṣya) and various epidemic fevers,
such as illnesses that recur every day, every two days, every three days, or every four days;
or constant fevers and extremely distressing fevers.
At that time, there shall arise diseases caused by *bhūta* spirits,
as well as diseases of wind, bile, phlegm,
and their combined humors; all fevers, headaches, and hemicrania.
May all [afflictions] be eliminated, including the diseases of stiffness and clouding,
eye diseases, nose diseases, mouth diseases, neck diseases,
heart diseases, throat pain, ear pain, tooth pain, and chest pain.
Pain in the head, pain in the flanks, pain in the back, pain in the abdomen,
pain in the waist, pain in the private parts, pain in the thighs, pain in the calves,
pain in the hands, pain in the feet, and pain in the limbs and joints.
May she eliminate [all obstacles] and protect me—Vajroṣṇīṣavijayā, the Mother of the Great White Parasol.
She binds the vajra boundary for twelve yojanas.
All bhūtas, vetālas, and ḍākinīs, as well as ghosts,
fevers, sores, scabies, leprosy, discharges, epilepsy, carbuncles,
itching, boils, dryness, and wind-induced seizures.
Poisons from jewels, poisons from insects, and calamities caused by fire or water;
resentment, enemies, harassment, untimely death, and sudden demise;
furthermore, there are poisons from *timapuṅga* bees, *tilaca* snakes, vipers, scorpions, and rats.
Dragons, tigers, lions, bears, brown bears, jackals, and wolves—
those who, like venomous bees, seize and harm one's life—
all such beings are completely bound and subdued by means of this vidyā-mantra.
Bound by majestic spiritual power,
bound by various vidyā-mantras,
and all malevolent spirits likewise bound.

*Tadyathā | oṃ anaile anaile | bhishte bhishte | nīra nīra | vajradhārī | bandha bandha | vajrabandhini phaṭ | hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ | hūṃ dhu ru ṃ bandha phaṭ svāhā.* If a person carries this *Buddhoṣṇīṣa-mahā-sitātapatrā-parājita-mudrā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,...
Having transcribed this upon birch bark, palm leaves, or plain cotton cloth,
if one wears it on the body or ties it around the neck,
it should be known that throughout the remainder of that person's life, no poison shall be able to harm them.
Furthermore, none of their weapons, water, fire, jewels, poisons, venomous insects, or malevolent incantations can cause them harm;
nor shall they suffer untimely death. As for all classes of ghosts and demons, [they shall likewise be unable to harm them].
All who see it will not fail to give rise to joy.
There are eighty-four thousand assemblies of Vajra-beings who,
filled with great joy, shall constantly provide protection.
Throughout eighty-four thousand great kalpas, they will attain the knowledge of past lives;
in birth after birth, they shall never be reborn among the evil destinies such as yakṣas, rākṣasas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, bhūtas, or other such spirits.
Furthermore, such a person shall not be born into poverty or low station,
but shall obtain a mass of merit from immeasurable, boundless Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
This applies to anyone who upholds this *Buddhōṣṇīṣa-sitātapatrā Aparājitā-mahāpratisarā Dhāraṇī Sūtra*.
Those who do not practice the holy life also accomplish the holy life;
those who do not maintain the precepts also accomplish the maintenance of the precepts;
those who are not pure also accomplish purity.
Even those who have not observed the *poṣadha* will accomplish the *poṣadha*;
even those who have not purified their fast will accomplish the purification of the fast.
This applies even to those with the five crimes of immediate retribution (*ānantarya*) or all manner of karmic calamities accumulated since beginningless time.
All past karma and accumulated sins shall be completely extinguished without remainder.
If there is a woman who desires to obtain a son and can receive and uphold this *Buddhōṣṇīṣa-mahā-sitātapatra-aparājitā-mahāpratisarā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, [her wish shall be fulfilled].
They shall give birth to sons endowed with wisdom,
whose merit, lifespan, physical appearance, and strength are all perfected;
after their lives end, they will accordingly attain rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Should one encounter human illness, disease among livestock, pestilence, affliction, strife, oppression by others, military incursions, or any other calamities,
this Great White Parasol of the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa is invincible to them all.
The Praṇamya-kīra-mudrā Dhāraṇī:
tie it to the top of a banner and extensively perform offerings as a great Buddhist rite;
then, to welcome this mantra, install it at the four gates of the city.
Whether in various settlements, cities, villages, or wildernesses,
if one pays homage, shows respect, and makes offerings with a single-minded heart,
all military arrays will immediately be extinguished.
May all pestilences, diseases, afflictions, harms, and strife;
the incursions and disturbances of enemy armies, and all calamities, be entirely extinguished.

*Tadyathā | oṃ anale anale | ghasami ghasami | nīra nīra | svāmi svāmi | sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhāna adhiṣṭhiteti | sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣasitātapatre hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | hūṃ mamā hūṃ ni svāhā.* If one is able to practice according to this Buddha[-teaching], [one shall attain success].
All the devas and nāga kings, in accordance with the proper seasons,
sent down sweet rain. At that time, all the Buddhas,
great bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, and so forth—
When the entire great assembly heard what the Buddha had spoken, they were all filled with great joy; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
*The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Great White Parasol of the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa*.
